mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille member-state route ONLY: notary public certification followed by a single apostille from the designated competent authority in the issuing country, then certified English/Korean translation; non-member-state route ONLY: notary public certification, foreign ministry legalization in the issuing country, consular legalization at the Republic of Korea Embassy/Consulate, then certified translation; the two routes are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille member-state route ONLY: authenticated corporate signatures, notarization, apostille; non-member-state route ONLY: authenticated signatures, notarization, foreign ministry legalization, consular legalization at the Republic of Korea Embassy/Consulate; apostille and consular legalization are independent and exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum and By-laws of the Investing Entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Investing entity or its notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille member-state route ONLY: notarized copy with apostille; non-member-state route ONLY: notarized copy, foreign ministry legalization, consular legalization by the Republic of Korea Embassy/Consulate; do not combine apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the Investing Entity's Relationship Bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Head office or authorized branch of the investing entity's relationship bank in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille member-state route ONLY: bank officer signature notarized and apostilled; non-member-state route ONLY: bank officer signature notarized, foreign ministry legalization, consular legalization by the Republic of Korea Embassy/Consulate; only one authentication path applies based solely on the issuing state's Hague Convention membership.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Passport / National ID Copies of Directors, Shareholders, and Beneficial Owners

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All ultimate beneficial owners, directors, and authorized representatives must be screened before incorporation against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN sanctions lists, the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) relevant warnings, the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctions list, EU and UK consolidated lists, and Interpol Red Notices. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for domestic, foreign, and international-organization politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates, and must include source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence. The NVOCC transaction profile also requires counterparty and transport-document screening for trade-based money-laundering red flags, front-company warnings, and merchant vessel ownership checks.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Commercial Registration Information System (Internet Registration Office)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name must be in Hangul script and must end with a Korean limited-liability designation romanized as Yuhan Hoesa. The English name is a secondary transliteration and must phonetically correspond to the Hangul registered name. The registration system applies a four-tier naming test: distinctive words, business-object words, liability suffix, and absence of prohibited or misleading tokens. Foreign investors must file the Hangul name and an approved English alias; any mismatch between the Hangul registered name and the English name used in shipping, customs, bank account, and NVOCC license documents may cause registration rejection and bank account failure.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A provisional name reservation may be extended once by resubmitting the pre-search request before expiration, attaching the original reservation certificate and renewed search fees. Upon rejection, within 14 days the applicant or a Korean-licensed attorney must file a written administrative appeal with the chief registrar of the competent Commercial Registration Office, including the rejected name, the pre-search certificate, and a legal memorandum showing compliance with Korean Commercial Act trade-name principles. The registrar must issue a written decision within 30 days, and if the appeal is denied the applicant may file an appeal with the High Court under the Administrative Litigation Act within 30 days of service, with the right to request an oral hearing and later judicial review.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or mere commercial mailbox is not permissible for a licensed Korean Yuhan Hoesa engaged in NVOCC ocean freight forwarding. The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries and the Korea Customs Service require an actual physical head office where original freight-forwarding records, bills of lading, customs declarations, service contracts, and compliance registers are maintained and available for inspection. The National Tax Service and Korean banks will reject a virtual address as proof of business premise; a valid registered office must be a leased or owned physical location, and the lease agreement and utility evidence must be presented during bank onboarding and NVOCC license inspection. A serviced office with dedicated licensed space may be acceptable, but not a mail-forwarding address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical inspection risk is high for a newly formed NVOCC licensee, estimated at 40% within the first 12 months of operation. Inspection checklist: Korean-language company name plate at the entrance; original Yuhan Hoesa registration documents and seal; Articles of Association and shareholder register; valid lease agreement in the company name; physical workstations and employee presence; NVOCC authorization; bills of lading and shipping documents for open files; client and carrier contracts; tax invoices and bank account statements; and AML/CFT training records. Failure of any checklist item may trigger permit suspension, tax audit, customs license cancellation, or criminal referral.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), particularly Articles 287-294 (incorporation of limited liability companies), Article 289 (articles of incorporation), Article 292 (registration), and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Act No. 5559) for non-resident investors.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division, District Court of the local jurisdiction where the registered office is located (e.g., Seoul Central District Court Registration Office).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (정관) and the Application for Corporation Registration (법인등기신청서) filed with the court registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) under the Commercial Act. However, for NVOCC licensing, the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries requires a minimum paid-up capital of KRW 100,000,000 (approx. USD 75,000) and a financial guarantee of KRW 100,000,000. These funds must be deposited in a domestic bank account and remain unencumbered during the license period.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, that the Board of Directors of Yuhan Hoesa (the 'Company'), acting pursuant to the provisions of the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea and the Company's Articles of Incorporation, hereby adopts the following resolutions as of the date of this meeting:

1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: The Board acknowledges that the initial share capital of the Company has been fully subscribed by the founding shareholders as set forth in the Subscription List attached hereto. The total issued and paid-up capital is KRW 100,000,000 (one hundred million Korean Won), divided into 10,000 ordinary shares of KRW 10,000 each. The Board confirms that all subscription amounts have been fully paid into the Company's designated escrow account at a licensed commercial bank, and that the bank's certificate of deposit has been obtained and shall be filed with the registry.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Board hereby authorizes the Chief Executive Officer and the Chief Financial Officer, jointly and severally, to open and maintain corporate bank accounts with any reputable commercial bank in the Republic of Korea. Such officers are authorized to execute all necessary account opening documents, signatory cards, and electronic banking agreements, and to designate authorized signatories for the purpose of wire transfers, ACH transactions, and other payment rails. The Board further authorizes the establishment of a dedicated operating account for the NVOCC business, subject to the financial guarantee requirements of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: The Board hereby adopts the registered office of the Company at [Insert Full Address, e.g., 12th Floor, Hanwha Building, 110 Sejong-daero, Jung-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea]. The Company Secretary is directed to file the registered office address with the court registry and to post the required notice at the office. The Board confirms that the registered office is a physical location where legal process may be served and where statutory records will be maintained.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: The Board hereby appoints the following individuals to the statutory offices of the Company: (a) [Name] as Chief Executive Officer, with authority to manage the day-to-day operations and to represent the Company in all business matters; (b) [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, responsible for financial reporting, tax compliance, and banking relations; (c) [Name] as Company Secretary, responsible for maintaining corporate records, minutes, and statutory filings; and (d) [Name] as Compliance Officer, responsible for ensuring adherence to NVOCC licensing requirements and anti-money laundering obligations. Each officer shall serve until their successor is duly appointed or until their resignation or removal.

5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: The Board authorizes the officers to take all necessary actions, execute all documents, and make all filings required to effectuate the incorporation, licensing, and operational commencement of the Company, including but not limited to obtaining the NVOCC license, business registration certificate, and tax identification numbers. The Board ratifies any actions taken prior to this resolution in furtherance of these objectives.

This resolution is effective immediately and shall be recorded in the minutes of this meeting. All officers and shareholders are bound by the terms hereof.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (공증인) and the Korean Legal Information Center (online portal for standard forms)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed Korean attorney to draft the Articles of Incorporation in compliance with the Commercial Act. The articles must include the company name (Yuhan Hoesa), purpose (including NVOCC and freight forwarding), registered office address, share capital, and number of shares. The document must be notarized by a notary public to confirm the identity and capacity of the incorporators. For foreign investors, the articles must be accompanied by a power of attorney and passport copies, and the notarization must be apostilled or consularized if required. Submit the notarized articles to the court registry as part of the registration package.
required_dossiers: Power of Attorney for each incorporator (if applicable)
Certificate of foreign investment registration (if applicable)
Proof of address for registered office (lease agreement or title deed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry rejects the articles due to defects, correct the deficiencies within 14 days and resubmit. If the rejection is based on legal interpretation, file an administrative appeal with the court or seek a declaratory judgment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Paid-Up Capital and Obtain Bank Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in Korea (e.g., Kookmin Bank, Shinhan Bank) and the Financial Supervisory Service (for AML checks)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary escrow account in the company's name with a licensed Korean bank. Transfer the subscribed capital (KRW 100,000,000) from the founders' accounts. The bank will issue a certificate of deposit (예금잔액증명서) confirming the balance. This certificate is required for the court registration. For NVOCC licensing, the same account must be maintained as a blocked account for the financial guarantee. Ensure that the source of funds is documented to satisfy anti-money laundering regulations. The bank will conduct a customer due diligence review, which may take 2-3 business days.
required_dossiers: Source of funds declaration and supporting documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays or rejects the account opening due to AML concerns, provide additional documentation of the funds' origin. If the bank requires a higher capital threshold, consider increasing the capital or obtaining a surety bond from a licensed insurer.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company with the Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division, District Court (e.g., Seoul Central District Court)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for corporation registration (법인등기신청) to the court registry where the registered office is located. The application must include the notarized articles, the bank certificate of deposit, the list of officers, and the registered office address. The court will review the documents for compliance with the Commercial Act. Upon approval, the court issues a certificate of registration (법인등기사항증명서). This step is mandatory for the company to acquire legal personality. The registration fee is approximately KRW 150,000 (USD 150). The process can be completed online via the court's e-registration system (인터넷등기소).
required_dossiers: List of officers (CEO, CFO, etc.) with consent forms
Registered office lease agreement or title deed
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a correction order, rectify the specified defects within 14 days. If the registration is refused, file an objection with the court within 14 days. If the refusal is based on substantive legal issues, seek judicial review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Business Registration Certificate from Tax Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) – local district tax office (세무서)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After court registration, apply for a business registration certificate (사업자등록증) from the local tax office. This certificate is required for tax purposes, opening bank accounts, and issuing invoices. The application must include the court registration certificate, articles of incorporation, and identification of the CEO. The NTS will issue the certificate within 3-5 business days. The company must also register for value-added tax (VAT) and corporate income tax. For NVOCC, the tax office will assign a business code (e.g., 5229) and may require additional documentation for the freight forwarding activity.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office requests additional information, provide the requested documents within 10 days. If the certificate is delayed, escalate to the NTS customer service or file a complaint with the National Tax Service Ombudsman.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for NVOCC License from Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (MOF) – International Freight Forwarding Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for registration as an International Freight Forwarder (NVOCC) under the International Maritime Transport Act. The application must include the business registration certificate, proof of paid-up capital (KRW 100 million), a financial guarantee (bank guarantee or surety bond) of KRW 100 million, and a detailed business plan. The MOF will review the application and may conduct an on-site inspection of the registered office. The license is valid for 5 years and must be renewed. The application fee is KRW 50,000. The MOF aims to process applications within 30 days, but the actual time may vary.
required_dossiers: Financial guarantee (bank guarantee or surety bond)
List of officers and their qualifications
Certificate of no criminal record for officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the MOF requests additional information, respond within 15 days. If the application is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the MOF within 30 days. If the rejection is based on capital or guarantee deficiencies, rectify the financials and resubmit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (MOF) – International Freight Forwarding Division; also the Korea Maritime Institute for advisory compliance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: International Freight Forwarder Registration (NVOCC License) under the International Maritime Transport Act (Act No. 15163)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (MOE) – Environmental Impact Assessment Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable – The business is a non-physical service (freight forwarding and NVOCC) with no manufacturing, chemical processing, or warehousing operations. No EIA is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable – No wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste generation. The company must still comply with general waste disposal regulations for office waste and electronic waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable – No physical premises beyond a standard office. The company must obtain a basic fire safety certificate from the local fire station for the registered office, which is a routine inspection. No special civil defense permits are required. The company must also register with the Ministry of Employment and Labor for workplace safety insurance (산재보험) and provide a safe working environment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, operating the HomeTax electronic portal (www.hometax.go.kr); customs and export declaration filing is administered by the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS system (unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity establishing a Korean Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) must first complete incorporation under the Korean Commercial Act and register the corporation at the local court registry. The foreign investment must then be reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, usually through a KOTRA investment support center or the Trade-Korea single-window portal. Tax registration is obtained by filing a business registration application with the district tax office of the National Tax Service having jurisdiction over the registered head office. The application must be submitted within one month of the commencement of business and accompanied by the articles of incorporation, certificate of corporate registration, evidence of the domestic place of business (lease agreement or title deed), the foreign parent entity's certificate of incorporation or equivalent legal existence document, board resolution appointing a domestic tax representative or statutory representative, and a power of attorney if using a certified tax agent. The NTS then issues a Business Registration Certificate containing the unique Business Registration Number (TIN), which also functions as the value-added tax (VAT) registration number. For a non-resident seller of services or digital goods without a domestic fixed place of business, a domestic tax representative must be appointed to complete VAT registration and file returns through HomeTax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea does not operate a US-style check-the-box election. A Korean domestic Yuhan Hoesa is treated as a domestic corporation taxed at the entity level under the Corporate Tax Act. There is no statutory mechanism to elect pass-through treatment or territorial scope for a domestic LLC. Hybrid mismatch rules under the Adjustment of International Tax Act apply to address double-deduction and deduction-without-inclusion outcomes, but no elective safe harbour is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary turnover exemption threshold for VAT registration. Any person making taxable supplies of goods or services in Korea as a business owner must register with the National Tax Service. A simplified taxable person regime applies when the previous calendar-year taxable turnover is below KRW 30,000,000, but registration remains mandatory and the simplified regime affects remittance and invoicing mechanics only, not the existence of a tax registration obligation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All registered Korean VAT entrepreneurs must issue electronic tax invoices (e-Tax Invoices) through the NTS HomeTax electronic invoicing system. The e-Tax Invoice must be transmitted to the National Tax Service by the end of the day following the date of supply. There is no general third-party anti-fraud digital stamping regime in Korean VAT; transaction integrity is protected by NTS-issued digital signatures, the mandatory electronic transmission channel, and the HomeTax cross-matching database. Taxpayers may use the NTS HomeTax web interface or the NTS Open API for machine-to-machine electronic invoice filing and clearance-related data exchange.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% VAT applies to exported goods where the goods are removed from Korea under an accepted export declaration; services performed wholly outside Korea; international transportation of goods or passengers; and other foreign-exchange-earning services provided to non-residents, including qualifying international freight forwarding. For an NVOCC ocean freight forwarder, the freight forwarding commission or net fee qualifies as zero-rated only where the service is genuinely connected to international ocean carriage, evidenced by a carrier master bill of lading or a recognized house bill of lading issued by the NVOCC, proof of actual international movement of the cargo, and a direct payment or invoicing link to the foreign counterparty. Merely incidental inland handling, warehousing, or port services that are not internationally connected remain subject to standard-rate VAT at 10%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export Declaration submitted to the Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS (the statutory Korean export declaration equivalent to a Bill of Entry)
Ocean Bill of Lading or NVOCC House Bill of Lading evidencing actual international carriage
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or Foreign Exchange Bank Receipt Certification showing the export sales proceeds have been received from outside Korea
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Tax Service and Korea Customs Service may jointly audit export transactions and require production of the export declaration, bill of lading, invoice, and foreign exchange receipt documentation. If zero-rated export treatment is found to be fraudulent, unsubstantiated, or not supported by actual foreign reimbursement within the statutory period, the NTS will retroactively assess the unpaid 10% VAT, impose additional tax penalties under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, and may impose criminal fines or imprisonment for intentional tax evasion. The taxpayer bears the burden of maintaining a complete documentary chain for at least five years from the date of export.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK), operating in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the Foreign Exchange Administration under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea operates a broadly liberalised but report-heavy foreign exchange control regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. The Korean won is fully convertible for most current-account transactions, including trade in services, freight forwarding, and remittance of dividends, provided the transaction has a genuine underlying commercial purpose and is reported to the registered foreign-exchange bank. Capital-account transactions are free in principle under the positive system but require prior or post facto reporting, as applicable. Export proceeds do not have to be surrendered into won; however, they must be collected through a licensed foreign-exchange bank within statutory periods and either held in a domestic foreign-currency account or converted to KRW. Profit remittance for non-resident shareholders is generally permissible after tax clearance, but banks will require documentary evidence of underlying earnings, certified financial statements, tax payment confirmations, and board resolutions. Practical hurdles are not regulatory convertibility limits but strict AML/KYC documentation, beneficial ownership certification, tax withholding, and Korea's real-name financial transaction verification. Overall, South Korea is assessed as a highly convertible jurisdiction with high compliance intensity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be received within 18 months from the date of export declaration; if the goods are shipped after the export declaration, the period runs from the shipment date. Extension of up to 6 months is available with the approval of the relevant foreign exchange bank for justifiable causes. There is no mandatory conversion ratio; exporters may retain proceeds in foreign currency, but must deposit them in a domestic foreign-exchange bank account and report settlement through the Korea Foreign Exchange Information System (KFIS).

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low - not viable as a standalone banking relationship. Under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, foreign fintech EMI companies without a domestic bank license cannot open Korean-won settlement accounts or act as licensed foreign exchange banks. They may only provide payment aggregation if they partner with a licensed Korean bank; in practice, no standalone foreign EMI account will satisfy statutory requirements for corporate FX reporting or capital-account movement. Direct Tier-1 domestic bank onboarding is mandatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical visit by the statutory representative or a formally appointed domestic director is the baseline requirement for corporate account opening. Remote consular proxy opening is not a statutory right and is permitted only on a bank-by-bank exception basis with enhanced due diligence; many banks require physical appearance at the designated branch for the KYC interview. Non-resident directors may delegate treasury authority to a resident signatory, but beneficial ownership and economic substance documentation must still be submitted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership and control opacity for a newly formed Korean LLC with non-resident shareholders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and apostilled corporate registry certificates, shareholders' register, UBO declaration on the bank's prescribed form, passport copies of all directors and UBOs, executed power of attorney, and a corporate seal certificate confirming the authorised signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering indicators, including invoicing and freight-versus-cargo misalignment common in NVOCC operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: For the first 3 to 6 months of planned transactions: master bills of lading, house bills of lading, customs export and import declarations, packing lists, commercial contracts, carrier rate confirmations, independent freight quotations, and a written business model explaining commission and freight revenue logic.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, export-controlled cargo, or high-risk geographic exposure involving Iran, North Korea, Russia, Syria, Cuba, or other restricted destinations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OFAC/EU/UN and Korea sanctions screening policy, denied-party screening logs, cargo HS code classification with dual-use license determination, KYC files for counterparties and vessels including IMO numbers, AIS verification, and contractual end-use/end-user certifications.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds and foreign-exchange purpose code inconsistency on inbound capital injection from overseas investors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Share capital funding plan, bank reference from the remitting institution, Foreign Investment Report or capital transaction confirmation from the Korean bank, proof that the funding source is legitimately earned, board resolutions authorising the equity injection, and a projection of FX settlement purpose codes matching the NVOCC services.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection must be remitted via SWIFT MT103 from the investor's bank to the company's designated capital escrow foreign-currency account at a Korean licensed foreign exchange bank. The remittance instruction must carry the correct KFIS foreign-exchange purpose code corresponding to inward direct investment or equity acquisition. Upon receipt, the bank verifies the funds and provides a certificate of inward remittance / foreign investment registration. Under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, the foreign investor must file the investment report through KOTRA or the bank, and the company must obtain a Certificate of Foreign Investment Registration before converting the capital into Korean won for operational use. External auditors then use the remittance certificate, exchange-rate confirmation, and bank statement for capital verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for freight forwarding should be executed via SWIFT MT103 for direct remittance to overseas carriers, agents, terminals, and service suppliers; commercial documentary credits via SWIFT MT700/MT707 for large transactions; and documentary collections (D/P and D/A) for structured trade flows. All payments must be matched to the appropriate KFIS foreign-exchange purpose code for service payments or import settlement and backed by invoices, bills of lading, contracts, and customs declarations. Domestic Korean-won disbursements should use the certified bank ACH network for low-value operational payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore plain-vanilla forward exchange contracts for genuine trade and investment exposures
Cross-currency swaps, including FX swaps and currency interest-rate swaps, covering underlying freight receivables, payables, or debt service
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted for hedging Korean won exposure where physical delivery is not accessible or the counterparty is offshore
OTC Korean won currency options used exclusively for non-speculative risk management of confirmed commercial exposures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return and Financial Statement Attachments (balance sheet, income statement, and statutory schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Republic of Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after each fiscal-year end; for a calendar-year LLC closing on December 31, the filing deadline is March 31 of the following year. A one-month extension for domestic companies and a four-month extension for foreign-invested companies may be granted only with prior NTS approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Under-reporting triggers the National Tax Basic Act additional tax of 20% (negligence) or 40% (fraud) of the unpaid tax; daily late-payment interest accrues at 0.025%; failure to file by the extended deadline leads to a deemed NTS assessment, compulsory seizure and auction of corporate assets, denial or withdrawal of tax clearance certificates, and administrative cancellation of the business registration for persistent non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surcharge Return (local income tax on corporate net earnings)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipal government of the registered office, collected jointly through the NTS filing portal in most jurisdictions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as the corporate income tax return: March 31 following the calendar-year end for a December 31 fiscal year; extensions mirror the corporate tax extension.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid local income tax incurs a monthly 0.75% overdue surcharge with a maximum of 8.25% under the Local Tax Act, plus enforced municipal collection; prolonged delinquency can lead to seizure of assets and cancellation of the local business-registration entry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Preliminary Value-Added Tax (VAT) Return for January 1 - March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by April 25 of the same tax year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omitted or under-reported output VAT attracts a 20% additional tax; non-issuance of tax invoices attracts an additional 30% penalty; overdue VAT accrues daily interest at 0.025%; repeated material defaults may result in criminal referral and forced collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Final Value-Added Tax (VAT) Return for April 1 - June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by July 25 of the same tax year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omitted or under-reported output VAT attracts a 20% additional tax; non-issuance of tax invoices attracts an additional 30% penalty; overdue VAT accrues daily interest at 0.025%; repeated material defaults may result in criminal referral and forced collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Preliminary Value-Added Tax (VAT) Return for July 1 - September 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by October 25 of the same tax year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omitted or under-reported output VAT attracts a 20% additional tax; non-issuance of tax invoices attracts an additional 30% penalty; overdue VAT accrues daily interest at 0.025%; repeated material defaults may result in criminal referral and forced collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Final Value-Added Tax (VAT) Return for October 1 - December 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due by January 25 of the immediately following tax year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omitted or under-reported output VAT attracts a 20% additional tax; non-issuance of tax invoices attracts an additional 30% penalty; overdue VAT accrues daily interest at 0.025%; repeated material defaults may result in criminal referral and forced collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory External Auditor Appointment and Independent Audit Report Filing (only if the LLC meets the audit thresholds set out in the statutory audit mandate)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Services Commission (FSC) through the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA); the NTS receives the audited financial statements as part of the corporate income tax return.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The independent auditor must be appointed at the ordinary members' meeting by March 31 for a calendar-year entity; the signed audit report must be delivered to the FSC/KICPA within two weeks after audit completion and in all cases before the statutory corporate return due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an auditor within the legal period is punishable by a punitive fine of up to KRW 50 million for the responsible corporate officer and may invalidate the financial statements for tax and financing purposes; the FSC may impose corrective orders and refer the matter for criminal sanction.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary General Meeting of Members and Approval of Annual Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: The company's registered office, where the minutes and financial statements must be physically available; no court or government filing fee is required unless a corporate change is concurrently registered.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year, i.e., by March 31 for a December 31 year-end, unless the articles of incorporation define an earlier date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delay in holding the ordinary members' meeting exposes each delegated member or manager to a Commercial Act administrative fine of up to KRW 10 million, prevents lawful recognition of the annual accounts, and allows any member to petition the court for an order convening the meeting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report on the Operation of the Foreign-Invested Enterprise and Standstill of Foreign Shareholdings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) through KOTRA, and the Bank of Korea for foreign-exchange direct-investment statistics
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 90 days after the end of the foreign-invested enterprise's fiscal year (by March 31 for a calendar-year entity). Any equity transfer involving a non-resident must be separately reported within 30 days of the transfer.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted filing of the operation report may trigger an administrative fine of up to KRW 10 million; unreported equity transfers may attract fines up to KRW 50 million, loss of foreign-invested enterprise status, restrictions on repatriation of proceeds, and delayed recognition in the statutory members' register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree, a Yuhan Hoesa LLC is legally obliged to appoint an independent certified public accountant and licensed CPA firm if any of the following quantitative thresholds is met: (a) the LLC's balance-sheet total assets at the immediately preceding fiscal-year end are at least KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.2 million at KRW 1,300/USD); (b) the LLC has total assets of at least KRW 7 billion and annual turnover of at least KRW 30 billion; (c) the LLC has total assets of at least KRW 7 billion and an average headcount of at least 300 full-time employees; (d) the LLC is a holding company, financial company, or state-invested company with total assets of at least KRW 5 billion irrespective of turnover or headcount; or (e) the LLC's ocean freight forwarding/NVOCC license holder status is declared a public-interest business by the Financial Services Commission. An LLC falling below all thresholds is exempt unless the articles of incorporation impose a voluntary audit. Measured at the immediately preceding fiscal-year end.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Accounting records must be maintained under the Korean Commercial Act and the KICPA professional standards framework. Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) apply to listed and public-interest entities. A non-listed Yuhan Hoesa LLC may apply Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP) or voluntarily adopt K-IFRS; if the NVOCC entity is consolidated into a foreign parent group, the Philippine? No, the group will require K-IFRS or parent-standard adjustment schedules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Republic of Korea does not operate a standalone annual UBO registry filing for an ordinary LLC. Instead, under the Financial Transaction Reports Act and the Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information, the Yuhan Hoesa LLC must identify and verify each natural person who ultimately owns or controls 25% or more of its share capital or exercises effective control by any means. This verification is performed at account-opening and updated on a change-driven basis. For shareholding transfers, the LLC must update its statutory Register of Members within 30 days of the transfer; where the transferee is a non-resident, the foreign-exchange acquisition/change report must be submitted to the Bank of Korea through a foreign exchange bank within 30 days. No separate annual member declaration is filed with the court.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (member/shareholder ledger maintained at the registered office)
Register of Directors (where directors are appointed under the LLC articles)
Register of Charges/Mortgages and registered encumbrances

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.4% aggregate top rate (24% national corporate income tax plus 2.4% local income tax surtax; progressive national brackets 9%, 19%, 21%, 24%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign-invested NVOCC/logistics operations in Free Economic Zones and Free Trade Zones may obtain corporate tax holidays of 100% for 5 years and 50% for 2 years under the Special Tax Treatment Control Law; additional R&D and facility investment tax credits, accelerated depreciation, and customs-duty exemptions are available for qualifying logistics software or container-terminal equipment; no general patent box applies to freight-forwarding income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return on Taxable Base and Tax Amount (primary Korean CIT form), filed electronically through the National Tax Service (NTS) HomeTax mandatory e-filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal-year basis) with two semi-annual interim prepayment installments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: File within three months after the fiscal-year end; for a December 31 year-end, the deadline is March 31 of the following year, extended to the next business day if the due date falls on a weekend or holiday.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification block: trade name, business registration number, head-office address, consolidated group code, and the business scope code for ocean freight forwarding (ISIC 5229 / NAICS 488510).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean Yuhan Hoesa entity code and attach Annex 5 declaring each non-resident shareholder's name, country of residence, shareholding ratio, foreign registration number, and the underlying Foreign Investment Reporting notification. Providing an incomplete foreign-ownership disclosure is a first-stage red flag that converts every later dividend distribution into an unreported non-resident payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from NVOCC operations: ocean freight brokerage, consolidated cargo booking, container handling fees, and ancillary logistics agency income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean resident company is taxed on worldwide income, so invoices issued to non-resident shippers or foreign charterers are fully taxable in Korea. Report all Swift_Wire and ACH freight collections through the company bank account; failure to submit foreign bank statements or intercompany booking records allows the NTS to reconstruct income and impose the 40% fraudulent-filing penalty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible costs and operating expenses: ocean freight payments, terminal handling, container haulage, vessel space charges, agency commissions, insurance, and administrative overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disallow any expense paid to a non-resident related party unless the cost is substantiated by contracts, invoices, flow of services, and arm's-length benchmarking. Payments for non-resident head-office services, royalties for booking software, or interest on foreign shareholder loans must be separately reported on the withholding schedule and, if treaty relief is sought, supported by a Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership statement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before NOL carryforward, after adding back tax-adjusted items such as entertainment, donations, fines, and transfer-pricing upward adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When a foreign controlling entity is present, never use this line to offset taxable income with expenses booked to a shell intermediary that has no employees or business functions. The director must sign a declaration that the entity has actual economic substance in Korea, including core income-generating activities such as contract negotiation, cargo consolidation, and issuance of bills of lading; a false declaration triggers personal liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit and treaty relief line for taxes paid to foreign jurisdictions on foreign-source freight-forwarding, container-leasing, or overseas agency income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credits by attaching foreign tax returns and remittance evidence. Non-resident shareholders cannot use this line to reduce Korean WHT on dividends; the Korean company must withhold at 22% or the applicable treaty rate on all distributions and attach a non-resident declaration and shareholding analysis to justify the reduced rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Distribution block for dividends, deemed dividends, retained-earnings remittance, and withholding tax accountabilities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each dividend paid to a non-resident shareholder, decode the applicable DTA rate. Enter the gross payment, domestic WHT amount, treaty rate applied, and reason code. The non-resident's Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership form must be on file before filing; otherwise the reduced rate is denied and the under-withheld amount becomes a personal liability of the responsible director.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or failure to file triggers additional tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes: 20% of the unpaid tax for ordinary unfaithful returns and 40% for false or fraudulent returns. Overdue tax attracts a 0.025% daily surcharge from the due date until payment. Criminal thresholds under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act apply when fraudulent non-disclosure exceeds KRW 50 million; conviction carries imprisonment up to 3 years, aggravated to 5 years for evasion above KRW 300 million, and fines up to 3 times the amount evaded. The NTS may blacklist the company, restrict overseas travel of directors, and publicize the delinquency.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surtax) on gross dividends paid to non-resident shareholders; reduced to 5%-15% under DTAs for qualifying shareholdings.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder or corporation must: (1) obtain an original Tax Residency Certificate from the treaty jurisdiction covering the payment year; (2) execute a beneficial ownership declaration confirming that it is not a conduit or pass-through entity; (3) submit to the Korean withholding agent the official NTS Application for Exemption from Withholding Tax under a Tax Treaty before the payment date; (4) provide notarized Korean translations of business licenses and financial statements; and (5) file the withholding tax return by the 10th day of the month after remittance, applying the treaty rate only when every document is complete. If the statutory 22% WHT was withheld in excess, the non-resident must file a refund claim with the NTS within three years from the statutory withholding deadline.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Non-resident royalty and interest payments are subject to the same statutory 22% WHT (20% national plus 2% local surtax). Treaty rates in major Korean DTAs generally fall between 0% and 15% for interest and between 0% and 18% for royalties; every reduced-rate claim requires a Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial ownership form, and a functional risk analysis showing that the intangible or debt instrument is genuinely connected to the Korean NVOCC's business.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File preparation and submission is mandatory when aggregate annual cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 5 billion; Master File is required when such transactions exceed KRW 50 billion or where the consolidated Korean/MNE group revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion, subject to exceptions in the International Tax Adjustment Act.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not operate a standalone ESR code, but the NTS applies the equivalent substance-over-form doctrine, the General Anti-Abuse Rule, CFC rules, and OECD BEPS principles to deny treaty or transfer-pricing benefits to shell freight-forwarding entities. For an NVOCC, Core Income-Generating Activities are the negotiation of freight contracts, booking of vessel space, container consolidation, issuance of house bills of lading, invoicing cargo customers, and managing foreign-agency relationships. These CIGA must be performed by qualified employees with actual decision-making power in Korea; if a director signs a tax return asserting more than this, the false representation supports piercing the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / False Corporate Income Tax Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The director files a zero-tax return while the Korean NVOCC retains millions in freight-brokerage revenue, deliberately omits gross revenue and foreign shareholder details, and instructs the bank to split Swift_Wire receipts to avoid the KRW 50 million criminal referral threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of Articles 3 and 14 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and Articles 47-2/47-3 of the Framework Act on National Taxes: imprisonment up to 3 years (up to 5 years where evaded tax exceeds KRW 300 million), plus a fine up to 3 times the evaded tax; administrative additional tax of 40% of the unpaid tax and daily late-payment surcharge.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced because the Yuhan Hoesa is used as a cloak for fraud; the director is jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax, subject to civil asset attachment, NTS overseas-travel blacklisting, disqualification from management of foreign-invested enterprises, and a personal imprisonment sentence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Fraud / Offshore Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intercompany payments are made to a zero-tax Hong Kong entity for freight consulting without any actual service performance, no Local File is prepared to corroborate the TNMM benchmark, and the NTS cannot locate Korean employees physically performing the core income-generating activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of Articles 4, 5 and 12 of the International Tax Adjustment Act: the NTS re-determines the arm's-length price, disallows the deductions, and adds a 30% additional penalty on the adjusted tax, plus daily overdue interest; criminal referral applies if the transfer-pricing adjustment is accompanied by fraudulent declarations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the veil arises where the interposed shell lacks commercial purpose; the director must restore diverted profits from personal assets, faces a travel ban and IVTS Blacklisting as a high-risk tax delinquent, and may be sentenced to imprisonment for the false transfer-pricing declaration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Sanctions and Shell-Company Abuse in Ocean Freight Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The NVOCC uses Swift_Wire and ACH to settle freight invoices for a charterer listed on UN or OFAC sanctions lists, layers the container charges through unrelated logistics brokers, and accepts crypto-asset or substitute remittances to escape Customer Due Diligence and Enhanced Due Diligence obligations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of Article 4 of the Act on Regulation and Punishment of Criminal Proceeds Concealment and Article 9-2 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act: imprisonment up to 5 years, confiscation of freight proceeds, fines up to KRW 300 million, revocation of the NVOCC license by the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, and financial sanctions by the Financial Services Commission.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The company is deemed a facade used solely for sanctions evasion; directors face personal criminal conviction, civil forfeiture of assets located in Korea, overseas-travel blacklisting, disqualification from any maritime transport license, and imprisonment from 1 to 5 years depending on the amount laundered.
